analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift and the bounded addition patch. Existing tests cover authenticated reread before ready receipts (1843–1863), disk-reserve/write/shutdown failure barriers (2010–2171), staging reservation cleanup and EngineV2Bridge deadline refusal (2323–2483), shared-entry/request isolation (2605–2772), and whole-root TTL/budget eviction without epoch rotation (2855–3022). These align with T-041, TB-007 and A-001; the shown additions do not change authorization, attestation, transport encryption, credentials, privileged helpers or billing.
The added test beginning at HEAD 3140 expects a previously recognized file's corrupted header to invalidate its cached ownership verdict despite restored mtime; malformed files are then excluded from deletion. The partial following test expects replacement of a malformed lookalike by a valid block to trigger another read. These are test-only additions, with no independently supported security regression in the supplied evidence. BASE tests are surrounding behavior, not new controls or regressions.
Integration must examine the corresponding SSDWholeRootMaintainer implementation: whether cached header verdicts are bound to opened-file identity and sufficiently precise change metadata, invalidated on replacement or mutation, and remain safe across concurrent enumeration/read/unlink. Validate that memoization preserves T-041's accessible-volume TTL/budget cleanup and does not replace payload authentication or storage-volume validation. The remainder of HEAD 3140–3240 and production changes are not supplied here; tests alone cannot establish those contracts.
